claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game contains an abundance of cheaters using aimbots, wallhacks, scripts, and macros.

citations.review_text:
**Apex Legends** has some of the best movement and gunplay I've experienced in a battle royale game, but unfortunately, the overall experience has become increasingly frustrating.

The biggest issue is cheating. Running into suspicious players happens far too often, and it seriously hurts the competitive experience. Nothing is more discouraging than spending time looting and fighting your way through a match, only to lose to someone who appears to have an unfair advantage. Whether it's obvious aimbots, wallhacks, or other suspicious behavior, these encounters make ranked and even casual matches much less enjoyable.

Another problem is matchmaking. Many games feel unbalanced, with new or average players frequently matched against highly skilled opponents. Instead of close, competitive matches, it's common to be eliminated within minutes without having much of a chance to fight back.

Server performance is also inconsistent at times. Lag, packet loss, and connection issues occasionally affect matches, making the game feel unreliable during important moments. Combined with the cheating problem, it creates a frustrating experience that often outweighs the game's strengths.

It's disappointing because Apex Legends has excellent movement mechanics, unique Legends, satisfying gunplay, and one of the best ping systems in the genre. However, until cheating, matchmaking, and server stability receive more consistent improvements, I can't recommend the game in its current state.


『Apex Legends』は、バトルロイヤルゲームの中でも操作性や移動システム、銃撃戦の完成度は非常に高い作品です。しかし、現在のプレイ体験には大きな不満があります。

一番の問題は、不正行為を疑うプレイヤーが多いことです。苦労して装備を集め、終盤まで生き残っても、不自然なエイムや壁越しの索敵と思われる相手に倒されることがあり、公平な対戦を楽しめない場面が少なくありません。

さらに、マッチメイキングにも改善してほしい点があります。初心者や平均的なプレイヤーが、非常に実力の高い相手とマッチすることがあり、一方的な試合になってしまうケースもあります。そのため、実力差が大きく、理不尽に感じる試合も少なくありません。

また、サーバーのラグや接続の不安定さを感じることもあり、大事な場面で思うようにプレイできないことがあります。

本来であれば、キャラクターごとの個性や爽快な移動システム、優れた銃撃戦など、多くの魅力を持ったゲームです。しかし、不正行為やマッチメイキング、サーバー環境が改善されない限り、現時点ではおすすめしにくい作品だと感じています。

Apex Legends appeared out of nowhere in 2019 and quickly proved that there is still room for innovation in the crowded battle royale genre. Today, after many seasons and updates, it remains one of the best and most engaging free-to-play shooters, though it is not a game without its flaws.

What makes Apex shine?

Incredible Movement Fluidity: The movement system is absolutely top-tier in the FPS world. Dynamic sliding, climbing, using the environment to jump, and grappling hooks make the pacing blistering. Standing still in this game is a death sentence.

Fantastic Gunplay: Respawn Entertainment (creators of the Titanfall series) knows exactly how to create a satisfying shooting model. Weapons have weight, recoil patterns require practice to master, and every hit is immensely satisfying.

Legend Synergy: Each available character has unique abilities (passive, tactical, and ultimate), which adds a layer of depth typical of hero shooters. A well-coordinated team can combine these skills into deadly combinations.

Revolutionary Communication System: The famous "ping" system introduced by Apex changed the industry (and was quickly copied by the competition). Even without using a microphone, you can communicate flawlessly with randomly matched teammates.

The Main Pain Point:

Network Infrastructure: Here we come to the most crucial point – EA definitely could and should do a much better job with their servers. This is the biggest and most frustrating flaw of this production. In such an incredibly fast-paced game where split seconds decide the victor, the technical backend often cannot keep up with the action on the screen. Hit registration issues (so-called no-regs, where you see blood and hear the hit, but the game registers zero damage), lag, stuttering at the start of a match, or errors kicking players back to the lobby are a daily occurrence. The server infrastructure (with a 20Hz tickrate) simply falls short of the standards expected of a modern, espo…

One of the best movement shooters I've ever played... for the five minutes I'm actually shooting. The other twenty? I'm apparently enrolled in the National Hiking Championship.

Don't get me wrong—the core gameplay is phenomenal. Sliding down hills, climbing buildings, chaining movement tech together, and pulling off clean squad fights feels incredible. Every Legend brings something unique, the gunplay is responsive, and when your team is synchronized, Apex delivers some of the most exhilarating firefights in the battle royale genre.

But then the fight ends.

And you walk.

Then you walk some more.

Maybe you loot a building.

Then you walk again.

"Oh, the ring's over there."

Guess what?

More walking.

Some matches genuinely feel like a sightseeing tour of the Outlands. You'll spend ten minutes sprinting across mountains, ziplining through valleys, and debating whether it's worth looting one more supply bin—only to get deleted by the first squad you meet. It's almost impressive how efficiently the game alternates between "nothing is happening" and "your entire squad is dead in 14 seconds."

The maps are beautiful, don't get me wrong. Respawn absolutely nailed environmental variety, and traversing them with movement abilities is satisfying. But there are definitely sessions where I feel like I've completed my daily step count before I've even fired my second magazine.

Despite my sarcastic complaints, Apex remains one of the smoothest shooters available. The movement system is second to none, the Legends are well-designed, and every victory genuinely feels earned because of the game's high skill ceiling. I just wish there were slightly fewer moments where my biggest challenge is holding the W key.

Gameplay: 9/10 (fast, fluid, and incredibly satisfying)
Movement: 10/10 (best in the battle royale genre)
Gunplay: 9/10 (responsive and rewarding)

After a few years away from playing Apex Legends I decided to redownload the game and give it a go again after watching some of my favourite streams start playing it again as well.

Many changes have happened since I played last, but the core fundamentals of Apex has always stayed true. The adjustment of the TTK is what I noticed the most, as it no longer takes multiple clips to knock someone. The movement is still the Golden standard in Battle Royale games in my opinion. The looting system is still top tier, weapons are the most balanced I have ever seen in an online shooting game, OG characters are still playable, but I will say, the lack of different game modes is something that needs to be addressed, but then again, sometimes simple is best.

None the less, Apex Legends is still the best BR game to not only play but to watch as well. The comp scene is hella entertaining, you can find many amazing streamers to watch and interact with.
